**Chapter 3 Quiz**   \hspace{2in} Name: \hrule


**1.** A child bikes East on a straight path. The table below shows the child's position (in meters) at a few select times (in seconds).

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline
$t~$ time (s) & 24 & 26 & 124 & 126 \\ \hline
$x~$ position (m) & 101 & 109 & 820 & 830 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

**a.** Estimate the velocity at $t=25$ s.

\vfill

**b.** Estimate the velocity at $t=125$ s.

\vfill

**c.** Estimate the acceleration from $t=25$ s until $t=125$ s.

\vfill

**2.** A speeding car has a speed of 30 m/s. By slamming the brakes as hard as possible on dry asphalt, the car can decelerate (slow down) at about 10 $\mathrm{m/s^2}$. (Or, if the direction of travel is positive, the braking causes an acceleration of $-10~\mathrm{m/s^2}$.)

**a.** How much time elapses between slamming on the brakes and the car coming to a stop?

\vfill

**b.** While decelerating (in the time between slamming on the brakes and coming to a stop), the average velocity of the car is 15 m/s. Using the time you calculated in part (a), how far did the car travel while decelerating?

\vfill

**c.** If the speeding car slams into a tree, it goes from 30 m/s to 0 m/s in 0.05 seconds. Calculate the (average) acceleration experienced during the crash.

\vfill

**3.** An elevator begins at ground level. It travels up and down. The elevator's **position** ($y$ in meters) is plotted as a function of time ($t$ in seconds).

```{r,echo=F,fig.dim=c(6,4),fig.align='center'}
par(mar=c(5,5,1,0))
ts = c(0,1,4,5,12,13,15,17,18,19,20)
ys = c(0,1,7,8, 8, 7, 3,-3,-5,-6,-6)
plot(ts,ys,"n",xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(-10,10),xlab="time (s)",ylab="position (m)",cex.lab = 0.8,cex.axis = 0.8)
for(i in seq(0,20,1)){
  lines(c(i,i),c(-10,10),lwd=0.5,col="grey")
}
for(i in -10:10){
  lines(c(0,20),c(i,i),lwd=0.5,col="grey")
}
for(i in seq(0,20,5)){
  lines(c(i,i),c(-10,10),lwd=1,col="darkgrey")
}
for(i in seq(-20,20,5)){
  lines(c(0,20),c(i,i),lwd=1,col="darkgrey")
}
abline(h=0,lwd=1.5)
points(ts,ys,cex=0.7,pch=19)
lines(ts,ys,lwd=3)
```

**a.** When $t=3$, what is the position of the elevator? \vfill

**b.** When $t=3$, what is the velocity (speed and direction) of the elevator?  \vfill

**c.** During which time interval(s) is the elevator above ground level (when is $y>0$)? \vfill

**d.** During which time interval(s) is the elevator moving up? \vfill

**e.** During which time interval(s) is the elevator stationary (not moving)? \vfill


\newpage



**4.** A dog runs North and South along a beach. Let positive velocity indicate the dog is running North.


```{r,echo=F,fig.dim=c(6,4),fig.align='center'}
par(mar=c(5,5,1,0))
ts = c(0,1,3,5,6,7,10,11,12,14,16,20)
ys = c(0,0,8,8,10,10,1,0,0,-6,-7,-7)
plot(ts,ys,"n",xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(-10,10),xlab="time (s)",ylab="velocity (m/s)",cex.lab = 0.8,cex.axis = 0.8)
for(i in seq(0,20,1)){
  lines(c(i,i),c(-10,10),lwd=0.5,col="grey")
}
for(i in -10:10){
  lines(c(0,20),c(i,i),lwd=0.5,col="grey")
}
for(i in seq(0,20,5)){
  lines(c(i,i),c(-10,10),lwd=1,col="darkgrey")
}
for(i in seq(-20,20,5)){
  lines(c(0,20),c(i,i),lwd=1,col="darkgrey")
}
abline(h=0,lwd=1.5)
points(ts,ys,cex=0.7,pch=19)
lines(ts,ys,lwd=3)
```


**a.** What is the velocity (speed and direction) at $t=8$ s? \vfill

**b.** What is the acceleration at $t=8$ s? \vfill

**c.** When is the dog stationary (not moving)? \vfill

**d.** When is the dog moving North? \vfill

**5.** A salmon swims 4 m/s relative to the surrounding water. The water is flowing North at 3 m/s.


**a.** Relative to ground, what is the velocity of the salmon when the salmon swims **South** at 4 m/s relative to the water? Please draw a diagram of vector addition.\vfill

**b.** Relative to ground, what is the velocity of the salmon when the salmon swims **North** at 4 m/s relative to the water? Please draw a diagram of vector addition. \vfill 

**c.** Relative to ground, what is the velocity of the salmon when the salmon swims **East** at 4 m/s relative to the water? Please draw a diagram of vector addition. \vfill
